inputs.root_cause: UblDocument had no version-related field or accessor at all: cbc:UBLVersionID was checked inline, ad hoc, only inside validate() (hardcoded to require exactly '2.3'), with no way for a caller to read the declared version as a first-class value, and no distinction between what a file originally declared and what the in-memory tree currently says after an edit. Identified as a concrete next candidate in FF6 Event 116, reusing the exact detected_version/declared_version design already built for NRRD-LIFECYCLE-001 earlier this session.

execution_steps: 1. Read model/document.py's UblDocument and model/__init__.py's document_from_root() (the parser's sole document constructor) in full, and confirmed all 91 generated root subclasses (model/root_types.py) are plain UblDocument subclasses with no extra fields, so a new base-class field propagates to every root type automatically.

2. Added ubl_version_id(root) -- a module-level helper in model/document.py scanning root.children for the first cbc:UBLVersionID child and returning its text -- and a new detected_version: str | None = None field on UblDocument.
3. Added UblDocument.declared_version as a live property calling ubl_version_id(self.root) -- always reflects the CURRENT tree, distinct from detected_version which is frozen at parse time.

4. Updated document_from_root() to compute detected_version = ubl_version_id(root) and pass it through to the document constructor -- the only call site of document_from_root() in the shipped namespace is the real XML parser (reader.py), so detected_version is correctly populated on every real load and left None on any hand-built document (UblDocument.build()), mirroring NRRD's reader-only assignment exactly.

5. Fixed with_root() (previously reset every edited document to source_sha256=None, signed_content_sha256=None with no detected_version parameter at all, which would have silently defaulted the new field to None on every edit): now explicitly carries detected_version=self.detected_version forward, so editing a document does not erase the memory of what was originally read.
6. Exported ubl_version_id from model/__init__.py and the top-level package __init__.py (matching the export pattern for other helpers like local_name/find).

7. Ran ruff, mypy, and the full ubl suite before writing any new tests to confirm zero regressions from the new field: 539 passed, unchanged (no existing test relies on UblDocument equality in a way the new defaulted field could break).

8. Wrote tests/python/ubl/test_obligation_detected_declared_version.py (10 tests): detected_version None on fresh construction, set correctly from a real parse (including a non-'2.3' value, proving it is not hardcoded), surviving a with_root() edit unchanged; declared_version reading the live tree, None when absent, changing independently of detected_version after an edit; the ubl_version_id helper matching the property. One test initially assumed dumps() would round-trip a non-'2.3' declared version byte-for-byte -- it actually raises UblWriteError, since dumps() validates before writing and the stable profile accepts only '2.3'. Corrected the test to prove REFUSAL rather than round-trip preservation: dumps() has no code path that could coerce an unsupported version to '2.3' and write anyway, which rules out silent substitution structurally, not just avoids it by convention -- an equally valid, arguably stronger, proof of 'never silently rewrite.'
9. All 10 passed after the correction. Re-ran the full UBL suite: 549 passed (539 baseline + 10 new, 0 regressions). ruff and mypy clean (25 source files).

evidence.why_this_is_real_new_code_not_evidence_c: UblDocument had zero version-related fields or accessors before this slice. detected_version, declared_version, and ubl_version_id are all new production code, plus a bug fix to with_root() (which would have silently dropped detected_version on every edit had it been added without this fix).
